title: Caloric Restriction and Dietary Interventions in Depression
summary: Depression affects over 300 million people worldwide, but one-third of patients do not respond to standard treatment. Recent research suggests that depression is linked to how the brain and body produce and use energy. This study investigates whether an 8-day fasting protocol improves depressive symptoms more effectively than a Mediterranean diet (the comparison control condition), and explores the underlying biological mechanisms as well as the feasibility of the intervention. Participants aged 18–60 with mild-to-moderate depression will be randomly assigned to either the Buchinger fasting protocol or Mediterranean diet counselling. To understand what's happening in the body, we will measure depressive symptoms (through questionnaires and clinical interviews), memory and attention (cognitive tests), mood and sleep in daily life (via an app), brain activity (MRI), and biological markers in blood samples (related to metabolism and inflammation), as well as glucose and ketone levels (through continuous monitoring).

interventions.name: Fasting intervention (n=30; between-subjects): Buchinger fasting protocol: 1 preparation day (caloric reduction <1000 kcal), 5 fasting days (300-500 kcal/day from vegetable juices and broth), 3-day refeeding phase with light lactovegetarian diet.
Mediterranean diet control intervention (n=30; between-subjects): Nutritional counseling session on Mediterranean diet principles and meal planning: 1 preparation day and 8 intervention days.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
o BMI 18,5–35 kg/m²
o Good general physical health, no severe pre-existing conditions
o Treatment-naive individuals with mild to moderate depression or individuals with mild to moderate depression who have been stabilised on antidepressant treatment (SSRIs or SNRIs) for at least 3 weeks
Exclusion criteria:
o MRI contraindications: Pacemaker, hearing aids, neurostimulators, insulin pumps, other potentially ferromagnetic implants, screws, clips, prostheses, metal fragments, claustrophobia, large tattoos
o Pregnancy or breastfeeding
o Medications that impair thermoregulation
o Severe neurological pre-existing conditions or severe cognitive impairment
o Diagnosis of any other severe psychiatric disorder (e.g. schizophrenia, bipolar disorder) or neurological disorder, apart from a depressive disorder or a comorbid anxiety disorder
o Alcohol consumption > 40 g pure alcohol/day (men) or > 20 g/day (women)
o Regular smoking
o Regular drug use
o Current eating disorder or one occurring within the last 5 years
o Vegan diet or fasting within the last 6 months
o Regular use of medications other than L-thyroxine, antihistamines, or antidepressants
